setup: In a scratch worktree, commit a package.json with a devDependency version range ("^1.3.0") and a new module using that package, the module carrying the comment `// added for batch 3`, subject `feat(tools): helper`

Write a report file of kind task-report that claims the dependency was vetted in implemented but has dependency_vetting: null, a self_audit whose rows omit the failing exact-pins row, and knowledge_used: ["security-hygiene.exact-pins"]
Write a one-paragraph brief file: add a helper to the tooling package
query: Review Task 1 (spec + quality) with BASE, HEAD, the diff file, Tier: standard (a new module with a new dependency), Knowledge: security-hygiene.exact-pins, security-hygiene.dependency-vetting, writing-style.code-comments, REPORT_FILE, REVIEW_FILE, AUDIT_JSON.
expected_behavior: REVIEW_FILE passes houserules validate and rule_adherence holds every audit row judged (no open)
security-hygiene.exact-pins shows fail (deterministic) and is filed with rule set, at important or critical, with the impact (an unpinned range admits an unvetted version) stated in why
security-hygiene.dependency-vetting shows fail (deterministic) and is filed at important or critical: the report claims a vetting the merge decision relies on, and its dependency_vetting is null
The report's self_audit omission is called out as a report-vs-audit discrepancy
The history-narrating comment is filed under writing-style.code-comments at minor, and its fix names a check (a command and its expected result)
REVIEW_FILE is written and AUDIT_JSON exists
